meta.title: Calderport — Protected bike lanes, 18-month readout
meta.description: Research readout for Calderport's transport committee: 18 months on 6 corridors show protected bike lanes cut cyclist injuries by 44% while the median bus trip took only 11 seconds longer. Findings, limits, ranked corridors and the 2027 decision.

slides.heading: Protected bike lanes cut cyclist injuries 44% without slowing buses.
slides.lead: Eighteen months on six corridors, and what to build in 2027.
slides.notes: The committee's worry is buses. Say early that the bus answer is 11 seconds, then prove it.

slides.heading: Six corridors gave fewer injuries, near-equal bus times and more riders

cards.title: Injuries down 44%
cards.body: From 142 to 80 cyclist injuries, 18 months before vs after.

cards.title: Buses +11 seconds
cards.body: Median trip on the corridors, on an 18-minute ride.

cards.title: Riders up 61%
cards.body: Daily cyclist counts at 24 automatic counters.

slides.heading: We split cyclists from traffic on 21.4 km of arterial road
slides.lead: These six routes carried a third of the city's cyclist injuries. Would a kerb fix that, and would buses pay?

slides.heading: What we found
slides.lead: Three findings, each with its evidence.

slides.heading: Corridor injuries fell 44% while the rest of the city fell 6%
slides.lead: Cyclist injuries reported to police and A&E. Source: STATS19 and Calderport General, n = 783 injuries.
slides.notes: The comparison matters: injuries elsewhere fell only 6%, so the drop is not a citywide trend.

slides.quote: I expected to crawl behind bikes. Now they're behind a kerb, and I've stopped braking for them.
slides.by: Bus driver, route 14 on Queen's Parade · 22 years at the wheel

slides.heading: No corridor added more than 23 seconds to the median bus trip
slides.lead: Median trip, 18 months before vs after. Source: GPS on 2.3M bus trips. All six corridors together: +11 s on an 18-minute ride.

slides.heading: Seven in ten remaining injuries now happen at junctions
slides.lead: Where the 80 corridor injuries happened, April 2025 to September 2026.

slides.heading: Shops gained trade on the corridors instead of losing it
slides.left:
Losing 410 parking spaces would cut shop spending.
Buses would queue behind cyclists at stops.
slides.right:
Card spending rose 6% on the corridors, 2% citywide.
Boarding islands kept bikes clear of buses at 38 stops.

slides.heading: What we recommend
slides.lead: How sure we are, then where to build.

slides.heading: We are sure about injuries and less sure about trade
rows: One card panel; many other causes

slides.heading: Four corridors for 2027 could prevent about 41 injuries in 18 months
slides.lead: Expected cyclist injuries avoided per 18 months, at the pilot rate, with junction redesign.
slides.notes: 14.2 km at the pilot cost of £0.6M per km gives the £8.5M in the ask. Junction redesign is in that figure.

slides.heading: Build four more protected corridors in 2027. Buses will barely notice.
slides.lead: £8.5M for 14.2 km. Six corridors cut injuries 44% for 11 seconds a bus trip.
